intro.text: You wake up on a cold stone floor. The room is dim — a single bulb flickers overhead. There's a heavy door to your left and a cluttered desk to your right.

insets.text: Location unknown. Time unknown. Duration unknown.

try_door.text:
The door is locked tight. You notice a small keyhole and a faint smell of rust. Scratches around the lock suggest someone else has been here before.

On the floor near the door you spot a crumpled note.

insets.text: The scratches are old. Many hands. Many attempts.

search_desk.text: The desk is covered in papers and old tools. Underneath a stack of manuals you find a brass key. There's also a battered logbook wedged between the drawers, and a half-written letter that ends mid-sentence: '...do not trust the—'

insets.text: The note said: key under the desk.

overlays.text: The tarnished silver watch sits in your pocket. Harrow knew someone would find it here. He left it for exactly this.

choices.label: Take the key and try the door
Read the rest of the letter carefully

read_note.text:
The note reads: 'Key is under the desk. Don't make noise. They patrol at dawn.'

Dawn. How long have you been here?

insets.text: No windows. No clock. The bulb has been burning the whole time.

choices.label: Search the desk for the key

read_logbook.text:
The logbook belonged to someone called Harrow — a prisoner here three years ago. The last entry reads:

'The night guard has a weakness for silver. I traded my watch and he looked the other way. The watch is still in the desk drawer if anyone finds this.'

You check the drawer. A tarnished silver watch is tucked under a cloth.

insets.text: Three years ago. Same room. Same door.

choices.label: Take the watch and return to the desk

read_letter.text:
You piece together the rest of the letter from faint impressions on the page below. It warns of a guard who locks this room from the outside — and that the window at the end of the hall is always left unlatched.

You now have two options.

choices.label: Use the key and take your chances at the door
Forget the key — go for the window

use_key.text:
The key fits. The lock turns with a satisfying click.

You ease the door open — and walk straight into the guard. He grabs your arm before you can react, eyes hard.

overlays.text: Harrow's entry surfaces: 'The night guard has a weakness for silver. I traded my watch and he looked the other way.'

choices.label: You reach into your pocket and produce the silver watch. His grip loosens.

caught.text:
'Going somewhere?'

His grip tightens. You don't get a second chance.

overlays.text: The watch is still in your pocket. You knew about it. You didn't use it.

bribed_escape.text:
The guard turns the watch over in his palm, weighing it. Then he steps aside without a word.

You walk out into the corridor. Then the courtyard. Then the street.

Harrow's note paid off. You made it.

window_escape.text:
You slip down the hall, keeping close to the wall. The window is exactly where the letter said — unlatched, open just enough.

You squeeze through and drop into the cool night air. Behind you, the building fades into darkness.

You made it.

insets.text: The window was always open. It just needed someone to look.
